```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| results: 'hide'

# Load packages
if(!require(pacman)) install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, here, janitor,gt,
               bslib, bsicons, shiny, sf, ggspatial, 
               ggrepel,plotly, reactable,
               ggpubr, htmltools)

# Load rgeoboundaries package which is not in CRAN
if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("wmgeolab/rgeoboundaries", force = TRUE)

# Load data
hospital_data <- readxl::read_excel(here("data/Healthcare Analysis Dataset.xlsx"))
head(hospital_data)

```


```{r}
# Calculate new variables required for analysis

# Calculate duration of hospital stay, age groups
hospital_data1 <- hospital_data %>% 
  mutate(hospital_days= as.integer(`Discharge Date`- `Date of Admission`),
        age_groups= case_when(Age <18 ~ "<18 yrs",
                    Age >=18 & Age <35 ~ "18-34 yrs",
                    Age >=35 & Age <50 ~ "35-49 yrs",
                    Age >=50 & Age <65 ~ "50-64 yrs",
                    Age >=65 ~ "65+ yrs"),
        DOA_year= year(`Date of Admission`),
        DOA_month=month(`Date of Admission`, label = TRUE))
```


```{r}
# Patient Demographics

# (1) By Gender
patient_gender <- hospital_data %>% 
  group_by(Gender) %>% 
  summarize(patient_number=n()) %>% 
  ggplot(mapping=aes(x=Gender, y=patient_number, fill = Gender))+
  geom_col(mapping=aes(text=paste("No. Patients= ", patient_number)))+
  labs(title= "Gender Distribution among Patients",
       x= "Gender",
       y= "Number of Patients")+
  theme(legend.position = "none")
patient_gender_plotly <- ggplotly(patient_gender, tooltip = "text")

# (2) By Age Groups
patient_age_groups <- hospital_data1 %>% 
  group_by(age_groups) %>% 
  summarize(patient_number=n()) %>% 
  ggplot(mapping=aes(x=age_groups, y=patient_number, fill = age_groups))+
  geom_col(mapping=aes(text=paste("No. Patients= ", patient_number)))+
  labs(title= "Age Distribution among Patients",
       x= "Age Groups",
       y= "Number of Patients")+
  theme(legend.position = "none")
patient_age_groups_plotly <- ggplotly(patient_age_groups, tooltip = "text")

# (3) By Admission Type
admission_type <- hospital_data %>% 
  tabyl(`Admission Type`) %>% 
  arrange(-n) %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  fmt_percent(columns = percent, decimals=1) %>% 
  cols_label(`Admission Type`= "Admission Type",
            n= "No. Patients",
            percent= "Percentage") %>% 
  tab_options(
    table.width = pct(100), # Makes it responsive to the dashboard card width
    row.striping.background_color = "#f9f9f9"
  )

# (4) Draw the map of hospital locations vs. patient load

# Calculate total patients per hospital
patient_load_per_hospital <- hospital_data %>% 
  group_by(Hospital, `Hospital Longitude`, `Hospital Latitude`) %>% summarize(total_patients = n())

# Change coordinates into sf object
hospital_location <- st_as_sf(patient_load_per_hospital, coords = c("Hospital Longitude", "Hospital Latitude"), crs=4326)

# Obtain the base map of US provinces
us_map <- rgeoboundaries::geoboundaries(country = "United States",
                              adm_lvl = 1) 

hospital_map <- 
  ggplot()+
  geom_sf(data=us_map)+
  geom_sf(data=hospital_location,
          mapping=aes(size=total_patients,
                      text = paste(Hospital, "<br>Total Patients: ", total_patients)), # add tooltip
          color="blue",
          alpha=0.5)+
  labs(title = "Number of Patients across 10 Selected Hospitals in US",
       x= "Longitude",
       y= "Latitude")+
  # map extent
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-125,-70), ylim = c(24,50))

# Give it to Plotly to create an interactive map 
# Note: geom_sf_text_repel cannot be used with Plotly
interactive_hospital_map <- ggplotly(hospital_map, tooltip = "text")

# (5) Health insurance providers
insurance_provider <- hospital_data %>% 
  group_by(`Insurance Provider`) %>% 
  summarize(patient_number=n()) %>% 
  ggplot(mapping=aes(x=`Insurance Provider`, y=patient_number, fill = `Insurance Provider`))+
  geom_col(mapping=aes(text=paste("No. Patients= ", patient_number)))+
  labs(title= "Insurance Providers of Patients",
       x= "Insurance Providers",
       y= "Number of Patients")+
  theme(legend.position = "none")
insurance_provider_plotly <- ggplotly(insurance_provider, tooltip = "text")
```

```{r}
# Patient Admission across Years (2020-2023)
admission_trend1 <- hospital_data1 %>% 
  filter(DOA_year != "2019" & DOA_year!= "2024") %>% 
  group_by(DOA_year) %>% 
  summarize(patient_number=n())
  
admission_trendline1 <- ggplot(data=admission_trend1,
       mapping=aes(x=DOA_year,y=patient_number, 
                   group = 1, 
                   text = paste0("No. patients= ", patient_number)))+ 
geom_line()+
geom_point()+
labs(title = "Admissions Trend (2020-2023)",
     x= "Year",
     y= "No. Admitted Patients")
 
admission_trendline1_plot <- ggplotly(admission_trendline1, tooltip = "text") 

# Patient Admission across Months (2020-2023)
admission_trend2 <- hospital_data1 %>% 
  filter(DOA_year != "2019" & DOA_year!= "2024") %>% 
  group_by(DOA_month) %>% 
  summarize(patient_number=n())
  
admission_trendline2 <- ggplot(data=admission_trend2,
       mapping=aes(x=DOA_month,y=patient_number, 
                   group = 1, #treat all those individual months as part of one single, interconnected group
                   text = paste0("No. patients= ", patient_number)))+ 
geom_line()+
geom_point()+
labs(title = "Admissions Trend by Month (2020-2023)",
     x= "Month",
     y= "No. Admitted Patients")
 
admission_trendline2_plot <- ggplotly(admission_trendline2, tooltip = "text") 

# Medical Conditions

medical_conditions <- hospital_data1 %>% 
  tabyl(`Medical Condition`) %>% 
  arrange(-n) %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  fmt_percent(columns = percent, decimals=1) %>% 
  cols_label(`Medical Condition`= "Medical Condition",
            n= "Patient Count",
            percent= "Percentage") %>% 
  tab_options(
    table.width = pct(100), # Makes it responsive to the dashboard card width
    row.striping.background_color = "#f9f9f9"
  )


# Factors Influencing Hospital Stay (LOS)

# Compare hospital stay among different medical conditions
LOS_by_med <- ggplot(data=hospital_data1,
       mapping=aes(x=`Medical Condition`, y=hospital_days,
                   fill = `Medical Condition`,
                   text=paste0("")))+
  geom_boxplot()+
  stat_summary(fun = "mean",
               geom = "point",
               size = 3,
               shape = 23,
               fill = "white")+
  stat_compare_means(
    method = "anova",
    label.y = max(hospital_data1$hospital_days, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05)+
  labs(title = "Comparison of Hospital Stay by Medical Conditions",
       x= "Medical Condition",
       y= "Length of Stay (Days)")+
  theme(legend.position = "none")
LOS_by_med_plotly <- ggplotly(LOS_by_med, tooltip = "text")

# Compare hospital stay among different age groups
LOS_by_age <- ggplot(data=hospital_data1,
       mapping=aes(x=age_groups, y=hospital_days,
                   fill = age_groups,
                   text=paste0("")))+
  geom_boxplot()+
  stat_summary(fun = "mean",
               geom = "point",
               size = 3,
               shape = 23,
               fill = "white")+
  stat_compare_means(
    method = "anova",
    label.y = max(hospital_data1$hospital_days, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05)+
  labs(title = "Comparison of Hospital Stay by Age Groups",
       x= "Age Groups",
       y= "Length of Stay (Days)")+
  theme(legend.position = "none")
 LOS_by_age_plotly <- ggplotly(LOS_by_age, tooltip = "text")
```

```{r}
# Cost Analysis

# Average Billing Amount
average_cost <- hospital_data %>% 
  summarize(mean_cost=mean(`Billing Amount`)) %>% 
  round(2)

# Highest Billing Amount
highest_cost <- hospital_data %>% 
  arrange(-`Billing Amount`) %>% 
  head(1) %>% 
  pull(`Billing Amount`) %>% 
  round(2)

# Lowest Billing Amount
lowest_cost <- hospital_data %>% 
  filter(`Billing Amount`>0) %>% 
  arrange(`Billing Amount`) %>% 
  head(1) %>% 
  pull(`Billing Amount`) %>% 
  round(2)

# Association between cost and hospital stay

# 1. Summarize data
plot_data <- hospital_data1 %>%
  filter(`Billing Amount`>0) %>% 
  group_by(hospital_days) %>% 
  summarize(mean_cost = mean(`Billing Amount`, na.rm = TRUE))

# 2. Compute Pearson correlation manually
cor_test <- cor.test(plot_data$hospital_days, plot_data$mean_cost, method = "pearson")

# 3. Format the text exactly
cor_label <- paste0("R = ", round(cor_test$estimate, 2), 
                    ", p = ", round(cor_test$p.value, 2))

# 4. Build the plot using geom_text instead of stat_cor
stay_cost_association <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = hospital_days, y = mean_cost)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "glm", se = FALSE, colour = "red",
              aes(text=paste0(""))) +
  # Add the text manually at the top left of the graph
  annotate("text", 
           x = min(plot_data$hospital_days) + 4, 
           y = max(plot_data$mean_cost), 
           label = cor_label,
           size = 4) +
  labs(title = "Association between Cost and Hospital Stay",
       x = "Number of Hospital Days",
       y = "Mean Cost (USD)")

# 5. Convert to plotly
stay_cost_association_plotly <- ggplotly(stay_cost_association, tooltip = "text")


# Association between cost and medical condition
medcon_cost_association <- hospital_data %>% 
  filter(`Billing Amount`>0) %>%
  ggplot(mapping=aes(x=`Medical Condition`,y=`Billing Amount`, fill=`Medical Condition`, text=paste0("")))+
  geom_boxplot()+
  stat_summary(fun = "mean",
               geom = "point",
               size = 3,
               shape = 23,
               fill = "white")+
  stat_compare_means(
    method = "anova",
    label.y = max(hospital_data$`Billing Amount`, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05)+
  labs(title = "Association between Cost and Medical Condition",
       x= "Medical Condition",
       y= "Cost (USD)")+
  theme(legend.position = "none")

medcon_cost_association_plotly <- ggplotly(medcon_cost_association, tooltip = "text")

# Association between cost and test results
test_cost_association <- hospital_data %>% 
  filter(`Billing Amount`>0) %>% 
  ggplot(mapping=aes(x=`Test Results`,y=`Billing Amount`, fill=`Test Results`, text=paste0("")))+
  geom_boxplot()+
  stat_summary(fun = "mean",
               geom = "point",
               size = 3,
               shape = 23,
               fill = "white")+
  stat_compare_means(
    method = "anova",
    label.y = max(hospital_data$`Billing Amount`, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05) +
  labs(title = "Association between Cost and Test Result",
       x= "Test Result",
       y= "Cost (USD)")+
  theme(legend.position = "none")

test_cost_association_plotly <- ggplotly(test_cost_association, tooltip = "text")

# Association between cost and admission type
admtype_cost_association <- hospital_data %>% 
  filter(`Billing Amount`>0) %>%
  ggplot(mapping=aes(x= `Admission Type`,y=`Billing Amount`, fill=`Admission Type`, text=paste0("")))+
  geom_boxplot()+
  stat_summary(fun = "mean",
               geom = "point",
               size = 3,
               shape = 23,
               fill = "white")+
  stat_compare_means(
    method = "anova",
    label.y = max(hospital_data$`Billing Amount`, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05) +
  labs(title = "Association between Cost and Admission Type",
       x= "Admission Type",
       y= "Cost (USD)")+
  theme(legend.position = "none")

admtype_cost_association_plotly <- ggplotly(admtype_cost_association, tooltip = "text")
```


# About Project

**Overview** 

This project explored 55,500 patient records from 10 major U.S. hospitals (2019–2024) to uncover trends and optimize healthcare outcomes.

**Research Questions**

- What are the demographic characteristics of the patient population across the 10 major US hospitals?
- What are the temporal trends in patient admissions over the study period?
- What is the distribution of hospital stay duration, and which factors drive this variation?
- What is the range of total medical costs, and what factors are associated with cost variation?

**Methods, Tools and R Packages Used**

**Methods:** Descriptive Statistics alongside some Statistical Tests where relevant to explore associations between exposure variables and outcome variables (length of stay, billing amount).

**Tools:** R and Quarto

**R packages:** tidyverse, here, janitor,gt,
                bslib, bsicons, shiny, sf, ggspatial, 
                ggrepel,plotly, reactable, ggpubr,
                rgeoboundaries, htmltools

# About data

The data used in the dashboard comes from Onyx Data DNA Challenges (Apr, 2025). For more information, check the official website [here](https://datadna.onyxdata.co.uk/challenges/). The dataset is shown below and can be downloaded as a csv file.

```{r}

library(htmltools)

htmltools::browsable(
  tagList(
    reactable(
      hospital_data,
      elementId = "hospital_data_table",
      searchable = T,
      filterable = T)))
tags$button("Download as CSV", onclick = "Reactable.downloadDataCSV('hospital_data_table')")

```
